title: First-quadrant Hom bicomplex of an acyclic source and injective terms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and work with $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed acyclic cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], and let $b\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $K^r=0$ for $r>b$. Let $J^\bullet$ be a cochain complex with $J^q=0$ for $q<0$ and each $J^q$ injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; no augmentation or acyclicity of $J^\bullet$ is assumed. The formulas
$$D^{p,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},J^q)\quad(p,q\geq0),\qquad D^{p,q}=0\quad\text{otherwise},$$
$$d_I(h)=h\circ d_K^{b-p-1},\qquad d_{II}(h)=d_J^q\circ h$$
with zero boundary maps define a commuting first-quadrant double complex of abelian groups [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Every row $D^{\bullet,q}$ is exact, including its left endpoint: for $p>0$ every $h:K^{b-p}\to J^q$ with $h\circ d_K^{b-p-1}=0$ has the form $h=g\circ d_K^{b-p}$ for some $g:K^{b-p+1}\to J^q$, and for $p=0$ every such $h$ is zero. The finite-diagonal total complex
$$\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}D^{p,q},\qquad d_{\operatorname{Tot}}=d_I+(-1)^pd_{II}\ \text{on }D^{p,q}$$
is acyclic.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, the Hom double complex and its other filtration, used in Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, zero abutment for an acyclic source. Explicit first-quadrant reindexing, injective extension at every row including its endpoint, and finite-filtration argument from the parent proof, old steps 3, 5 and 6.

proof.text: Composition of module-sheaf maps is additive in each variable. For $p,q\geq0$, $d_I^2(h)=h\circ d_K^{b-p-1}\circ d_K^{b-p-2}=0$, $d_{II}^2(h)=d_J^{q+1}\circ d_J^q\circ h=0$, and both mixed composites equal $d_J^q\circ h\circ d_K^{b-p-1}$. Across the boundary of the quadrant the relevant composites are zero. Thus these formulas give the asserted commuting double complex. Its degree-$n$ diagonal has only the terms $0\leq p\leq n$, and is empty for $n<0$. The stated total differential squares to zero: its mixed terms have coefficients $(-1)^{p+1}$ and $(-1)^p$ and cancel.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf; explicit reindexing and sign calculation

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$, $p>0$, put $r=b-p$, and suppose $h:K^r\to J^q$ satisfies $h\circ d_K^{r-1}=0$. By acyclicity, $\ker d_K^r=\operatorname{im}d_K^{r-1}$. The cokernel universal property therefore descends $h$ to $K^r/\ker d_K^r=\operatorname{im}d_K^r\subseteq K^{r+1}$ in the abelian category of module sheaves. Extend this descended map along the indicated monomorphism to $g:K^{r+1}\to J^q$ by the defining extension property of the injective object $J^q$. Then $h=g\circ d_K^r=d_I(g)$, while every such boundary is a cocycle because $d_K^2=0$. This argument uses sheaf quotients, not surjectivity on sections.

source.place: Tag 0135, definition-injective; the row-exactness calculation underlying sites-cohomology Tag 07AA, expanded from the definitions

proof.text: At $p=0$, the upper support bound gives $K^{b+1}=0$, hence $\ker d_K^b=K^b$. Acyclicity says $\operatorname{im}d_K^{b-1}=K^b$. Thus $h\circ d_K^{b-1}=0$ forces $h=0$ by the cokernel universal property. This is exactness at the left endpoint, whose incoming term is zero. Rows with $q<0$ are zero. Together with the preceding step, every row is exact in all integer degrees.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf; agent-supplied check at the top degree of the acyclic source

proof.text: Apply the second spectral sequence of the existing first-quadrant double-complex theorem to $D$. Its page is ${}^{\prime\prime}E_1^{q,p}=H_I^p(D^{\bullet,q})=0$ by the row exactness just proved. The page-to-next-page homology isomorphisms show inductively that all later pages and their stable entries are zero. The theorem identifies these stable entries with the associated graded pieces of the image filtration on $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ and supplies $F^0H^n=H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$ for $n\geq0$. Each quotient $F^iH^n/F^{i+1}H^n$ is zero, so $F^iH^n=F^{i+1}H^n$; descending induction from $i=n$ to $0$ gives $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)=0$. In negative degrees the total complex is zero. Thus it is acyclic. No cohomological property or augmentation of $J$ was used.
